summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low and inconsistent, with only 9 sessions logged and several multi-day gaps suggesting significant lifestyle or work stress. Sleep quality is chronically poor — most nights fall well below 7 hours, body battery frequently bottoms out below 30, and the last few days (Jul 27-30) show critically low sleep and near-zero body battery, indicating accumulated fatigue entering Week 6. The one positive signal is the 77km cycling session on Jul 20 and some open-water swim progression, but running volume is far below what's needed to build toward a sub-4h marathon in 192 days.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — with body battery at 2 and sleep at only 41 min on Jul 27, the Thu Jul 30 double session (strength + cycling) risks deepening a hole that will take weeks to climb out of; consider dropping one of those sessions tonight if fatigue is still severe.

Running consistency is the most urgent gap for the Feb 2027 marathon: you completed only 3 runs totalling ~16.5km in 4 weeks, whereas the plan requires 18+ km long runs every weekend — prioritise protecting the Sunday long run slots above all other sessions.

Your Jul 18 run at 179 bpm avg HR for a 5:02/km effort signals you're working at near-maximal intensity for what should be a moderate pace; keep all running sessions strictly in Zone 2 (≤150 bpm) until sleep and body battery consistently recover above 60.

Add a short 10-15 min evening walk or mobility routine on rest days to improve body battery recovery without adding training stress — your battery is frequently not recovering overnight, and light parasympathetic activity can help.

Begin pool swim sessions as planned — your open-water data shows pace of ~25-28 min/km which is very slow, and structured pool work with drills is the fastest way to improve efficiency toward the Ironman 1:50/100m target.
